key_insight: A NURBS-based level set and speed-method formulation enable robust, CAD-compatible topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff–Love shells without local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports lightweight shell design under uncertain loads and material properties while preserving accurate boundaries for CAD/CAM workflows.
method: Model single- and multi-patch shells using isogeometric analysis with non-matching meshes.
Compute volume-based shape derivatives via the speed method and obtain descent directions through a biharmonic equation.
Represent material boundaries with NURBS level sets and treat uncertainty using Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian random fields.
evidence_signal: Numerical single- and multi-patch examples reproduce literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined isogeometric approaches, according to the abstract.
watch_item: Monte Carlo sampling may increase computational cost; the abstract does not quantify runtime or sampling convergence.
paper_title: Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
